title: 5 Most-Common Drafting Mistakes Under BNSS (And How to Avoid Them)
notes: Listicle format. Each mistake gets ~200 words: what advocates do wrong, why it gets returned at filing counter, how to fix. Examples: citing IPC sections in post-July-2024 FIR drafts, wrong section prefix, missing electronic-evidence provisions, BNSS §35 arrest-procedure references.
body:
The transition to the new criminal codes, particularly the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS), presents a significant learning curve for advocates. While the foundational principles of criminal procedure largely persist, the renumbering of sections and subtle yet crucial procedural modifications demand meticulous attention to detail in your drafting. Errors, however minor, can lead to filing delays or even adverse judicial outcomes.

Precision in legal drafting is paramount. A poorly drafted document, be it an FIR, a bail application, or a challenge to an arrest, risks rejection at the filing counter or prolonged litigation. Understanding the common pitfalls under BNSS is the first step towards ensuring your submissions are legally sound and procedurally compliant.

You must adapt your drafting practices immediately to align with the new legal framework. This guide highlights five prevalent drafting mistakes observed since the implementation of BNSS and provides actionable strategies to avoid them.

## 1. Incorrect Statutory References: IPC/CrPC vs. BNS/BNSS

One of the most frequent errors is the continued citation of sections from the Indian Penal Code (IPC) and Code of Criminal Procedure (CrPC) for incidents occurring on or after July 1, 2024. Despite extensive awareness campaigns, many initial drafts submitted to courts or police stations still incorrectly refer to old codes. This oversight immediately signals non-compliance with the new regime.

**What Advocates Do Wrong:** You might draft an FIR or a complaint under "IPC §302" or file a bail application citing "CrPC §439" for a post-July 2024 offense. Similarly, references to the Indian Evidence Act, 1872, instead of the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA), 2023, are common.

**Why It Gets Returned:** Filing counters are instructed to scrutinize documents for correct statutory references. A document citing outdated laws for a new incident will be flagged and returned for amendment, causing unnecessary delays. Courts will also require corrections, potentially impacting the urgency of your matter.

**How to Fix It:** Always verify the date of the incident. For any matter originating on or after July 1, 2024, ensure every reference to substantive criminal law uses the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), and every reference to criminal procedure uses the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita (BNSS). For evidence-related aspects, cite the Bharatiya Sakshya Adhiniyam (BSA).

### Old vs. New Section Mapping (Examples)

| Old Code (Pre-July 2024) | New Code (Post-July 2024) |
| :----------------------- | :------------------------ |
| IPC §302 (Murder)        | BNS §101 (Murder)         |
| IPC §376 (Rape)          | BNS §63 (Rape)            |
| CrPC §41 (Arrest)        | BNSS §35 (Arrest)         |
| CrPC §154 (FIR)          | BNSS §173 (FIR)           |
| CrPC §439 (Bail)         | BNSS §482 (Bail)          |
| Indian Evidence Act §65B | BSA §63                   |

**Draft Sample (FIR Excerpt):**

```markdown
"दिनांक 05.07.2024 को, आरोपी [आरोपी का नाम] ने, ग्राम [ग्राम का नाम], थाना [थाना का नाम] के पास, फरियादी [फरियादी का नाम] को धारदार हथियार से मारकर गंभीर चोट पहुंचाई, जिससे उसकी मृत्यु हो गई। उक्त कृत्य भारतीय न्याय संहिता, 2023 की धारा 101 के अंतर्गत दंडनीय अपराध है।"
```

## 2. Overlooking Electronic Evidence Provisions

The BSA introduces significant changes regarding electronic evidence, particularly concerning its admissibility and the procedure for its production. Failing to address these new requirements in your drafting can lead to crucial evidence being deemed inadmissible.

**What Advocates Do Wrong:** You might simply mention "CCTV footage" or "WhatsApp chats" as evidence without considering the specific procedural safeguards required under BSA. Many drafts fail to include the mandatory certificate for electronic records.

**Why It Gets Returned:** Courts and investigating agencies, now operating under BSA, will strictly enforce the new provisions. If your application or complaint relies on electronic evidence without adequately pleading its compliance with BSA §63, it may be challenged or rejected. This can severely undermine your case.

**How to Fix It:** When electronic evidence is central to your case, ensure your drafting explicitly acknowledges its nature and, where applicable, states compliance with BSA provisions. For electronic records, always prepare and submit the certificate required under BSA §63. In applications for production of evidence, specifically request the electronic record along with the necessary certification from the custodian.

**Draft Sample (Complaint Paragraph):**

```markdown
"घटना का संपूर्ण विवरण आरोपी के मोबाइल फोन में रिकॉर्ड एक ऑडियो क्लिप में उपलब्ध है, जिसे भारतीय साक्ष्य अधिनियम, 2023 की धारा 63 के तहत प्रमाणित किया जा सकता है। यह इलेक्ट्रॉनिक साक्ष्य घटनाक्रम को स्पष्ट रूप से स्थापित करता है।"
```

## 3. Incorrect Arrest Procedure References: CrPC §41 vs. BNSS §35

Challenging the legality of an arrest or seeking remedies based on procedural irregularities requires precise statutory references. Misquoting the relevant section for arrest procedures under the new code is a common mistake that weakens your arguments.

**What Advocates Do Wrong:** In a habeas corpus petition or a bail application challenging the legality of an arrest, you might still refer to "CrPC §41" for arrests without a warrant, or "CrPC §50" for informing grounds of arrest. This demonstrates a lack of familiarity with the BNSS framework.

**Why It Gets Returned:** The Court will expect you to cite the current law. Arguments based on "CrPC §41" will be technically incorrect for post-July 2024 arrests. This can lead to a preliminary objection from the prosecution or a direction from the bench to amend your application, delaying the urgent relief you seek.

**How to Fix It:** Familiarize yourself thoroughly with BNSS Chapter V, which deals with arrest of persons. Specifically, BNSS §35 outlines the circumstances under which a police officer may arrest without a warrant, corresponding to the erstwhile CrPC §41. Similarly, BNSS §38 requires informing the person arrested about the grounds of arrest and the right to bail. Ensure these new section numbers are correctly cited in all your applications.

**Draft Sample (Bail Application Paragraph):**

```markdown
"यह प्रस्तुत किया जाता है कि आवेदक को दिनांक [गिरफ्तारी की तिथि] को बिना किसी वारंट के गिरफ्तार किया गया था, और गिरफ्तारी के समय भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता, 2023 की धारा 35 के तहत निर्धारित प्रक्रियाओं का पालन नहीं किया गया। विशेष रूप से, आवेदक को गिरफ्तारी के आधारों की सूचना भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता, 2023 की धारा 38 के अनुसार नहीं दी गई।"
```

## 4. Incomplete or Generic FIR/Complaint Details for Cognizable Offenses

The BNSS, like its predecessor, emphasizes the importance of a clear and comprehensive first information report or complaint. Vague or generic details can impede investigation and lead to delays in justice.

**What Advocates Do Wrong:** You might draft a complaint with insufficient particulars, such as omitting specific dates, times, or exact locations, or providing only a broad description of the offense without identifying the specific BNS section. For example, merely stating "मारपीट" (assault) without details that would attract BNS §107 (grievous hurt) or BNS §108 (causing hurt by dangerous weapons).

**Why It Gets Returned:** Police stations are often hesitant to register FIRs based on vague complaints as it can lead to difficulties in investigation and potential quashing petitions later. They may ask for clarifications or more details, delaying the registration process. Courts also expect a clear narrative of facts constituting a cognizable offense.

**How to Fix It:** Always ensure your FIR or complaint draft is precise and comprehensive.
*   **Specifics:** Provide exact dates, times, and locations of the incident.
*   **Narrative:** Detail the sequence of events clearly, outlining how each act constitutes an offense.
*   **BNS Sections:** Based on the facts, make a preliminary assessment and mention the applicable BNS section(s). Even if the police later change the sections, your initial drafting should guide them.
*   **Witnesses/Evidence:** Include details of any witnesses or readily available evidence.

**Draft Sample (Complaint Excerpt):**

```markdown
"दिनांक 12.07.2024 को लगभग दोपहर 2:30 बजे, ग्राम [ग्राम का नाम] स्थित [स्थान का विवरण] पर, आरोपी [आरोपी का नाम] ने जानबूझकर फरियादी पर लोहे की रॉड से हमला किया, जिससे फरियादी के सिर पर गंभीर चोट आई। यह चोट प्रकृति में गंभीर है और भारतीय न्याय संहिता, 2023 की धारा 107 के अंतर्गत 'घोर उपहति' की श्रेणी में आती है।"
```

## 5. Misunderstanding Changes in Bail Provisions and Application Drafting

While the core principles of bail remain, BNSS introduces subtle shifts in timelines and considerations that impact how bail applications are drafted and argued. Failing to incorporate these new nuances can make your application less effective.

**What Advocates Do Wrong:** You might draft a bail application under "CrPC §439" or "CrPC §437" and argue solely on the old precedents without considering the new procedural timelines or specific provisions under BNSS. This includes neglecting to mention the implications of BNSS §190 (police report submission timeline) or the expanded scope of anticipatory bail.

**Why It Gets Returned:** Courts expect arguments grounded in the current law. An application that ignores new BNSS provisions or relies entirely on CrPC sections for post-July 2024 cases will be seen as lacking. While the fundamental discretion of the court persists, a well-drafted application leveraging BNSS provisions will be more persuasive.

**How to Fix It:**
*   **Correct Sections:** Always cite the appropriate BNSS sections: BNSS §482 for anticipatory bail (corresponding to CrPC §438) and BNSS §479 for regular bail (corresponding to CrPC §437/439).
*   **Timelines:** Integrate arguments related to the new timelines for police investigation and submission of the police report under BNSS §190. For instance, if the investigation is delayed beyond the stipulated period, it can be a ground for bail.
*   **Specifics:** Emphasize the expanded grounds for anticipatory bail, particularly for women, children, and persons with disabilities, as articulated in BNSS.

**Draft Sample (Regular Bail Application Paragraph):**

```markdown
"यह निवेदन किया जाता है कि आवेदक को भारतीय न्याय संहिता, 2023 की धारा 101 के तहत आरोपित किया गया है। आवेदक दिनांक [गिरफ्तारी की तिथि] से न्यायिक हिरासत में है। भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता, 2023 की धारा 190 के अनुसार, पुलिस रिपोर्ट प्रस्तुत करने की समय-सीमा का पालन नहीं किया गया है, और आवेदक का आगे कारावास में रहना अनावश्यक है। अतः, आवेदक को भारतीय नागरिक सुरक्षा संहिता, 2023 की धारा 479 के तहत जमानत पर रिहा किया जाए।"
```
